item.title: Chandra OCR 2: Advanced Document Conversion and Extraction
item.description:
Chandra OCR 2: Advanced Document Conversion and Extraction

Chandra OCR 2, a state-of-the-art OCR model, has been released with significant improvements in math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR. It converts images and PDFs into structured HTML/Markdown/JSON while preserving layout information.

🔍 Overview

  • Chandra OCR 2 is a state-of-the-art OCR model that converts images and PDFs into structured HTML/Markdown/JSON while preserving layout information.
  • It has significant improvements in math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR.
  • The model supports 90+ languages and has excellent handwriting support.
  • It reconstructs forms accurately, including checkboxes, and has strong performance with tables, math, and complex layouts.
  • The model extracts images and diagrams, and adds captions and structured data.

⚙️ Key details

  • Chandra OCR 2 has two inference modes: local (HuggingFace) and remote (vLLM server).
  • Multilingual performance was a focus for Chandra 2. There isn’t a good public multilingual OCR benchmark, so the team made their own.
  • The model was benchmarked with the widely accepted olmocr benchmark.

🚀 Availability

  • Chandra OCR 2 is available for commercial self-hosting with a license.
  • For on-prem licensing, contact the team.
  • The Datalab API turns documents into verifiable knowledge your agents act on. Every result traces back to its page and position, and one API can parse, extract, fill and edit documents.
  • Get started with about 5,000 free convert pages every month (work email) — sign up — takes under 30 seconds — or try Chandra in the public playground.
  • If you have high volume workloads, a batch processing service is available that has processed 1B+ pages in a day at peak.

💡 Why it matters

  • Chandra OCR 2’s improvements in math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR make it a powerful tool for document conversion and extraction.
  • The model’s ability to preserve layout information and reconstruct forms accurately is particularly notable.
  • The availability of a batch processing service for high volume workloads ensures that users can manage their workloads efficiently.

📦 Installation 

1

pip install chandra-ocr

🔧 Usage

  • With vLLM (recommended, lightweight install)
1

chandra input.pdf ./output
  • Print Markdown directly to stdout
1

chandra input.pdf --stdout
  • With HuggingFace (requires torch + transformers)
1
2

pip install "chandra-ocr[hf]"
chandra input.pdf ./output --method hf
  • Interactive Web Viewer (zero extra dependencies)
1

chandra_app

📅 Timeline

  • 3/2026 - Chandra 2 is here with significant improvements to math, tables, layout, and multilingual OCR
  • 10/2025 - Chandra 1 launched

🌐 Multilingual Performance

  • The model supports 90+ languages.
  • Multilingual performance was a focus for Chandra 2.
  • The team made their own multilingual OCR benchmark to test tables, math, ordering, layout, and text accuracy.

📊 Benchmarks

  • Tops external olmocr benchmark and significant improvement in internal multilingual benchmarks.

📄 Document Conversion

  • Convert documents to markdown, html, or json with detailed layout information.

📝 Document Extraction

  • Extracts images and diagrams, and adds captions and structured data.

📋 Form Reconstruction

  • Reconstructs forms accurately, including checkboxes.

📝 Handwriting Support

  • Excellent handwriting support.

📊 Table Performance

  • Strong performance with tables, math, and complex layouts.

item.title: Rust‑Based docling.rs Speeds Up Document Conversion for LLM Pipelines
item.description:
Rust‑Based docling.rs Speeds Up Document Conversion for LLM Pipelines

The docling.rs project released a Rust port of IBM’s docling that delivers faster, lower‑memory document conversion for LLM and RAG pipelines.

🔧 Overview

  • Converts PDF, Office, HTML, scanned documents, and audio into Markdown, docling JSON, and other formats that LLMs or RAG pipelines can consume.
  • Produces output that is byte‑for‑byte identical to the original IBM docling implementation.
  • Operates as a single static binary – no Python runtime and no PyTorch dependency.

⚙️ How it works

  • Layout analysis, table recognition, and OCR are performed by built‑in ONNX models (layout, OCR, TableFormer, Whisper). These models are bundled (under 1 GB) and can be downloaded once via the provided scripts.
  • Office, HTML, Markdown, and e‑mail formats require no ML models.
  • PDF, images, and audio trigger the ONNX models for full‑fidelity extraction.

🚀 Performance

Format Speedup vs. Python docling RAM usage
PDF 4.3× faster under half
Office & HTML 20–60× faster —
  • Table extraction retains structure with cell recall 0.94, compared to MarkItDown’s 0.31 (see numbers).

🔗 Compatibility with existing stacks

  • MarkItDown: pip install docling-rs and replace the import with from docling_rs.markitdown import MarkItDown. All original formats, layout analysis, tables, and OCR remain functional.
  • Marker: Swap imports to from docling_rs.marker.converters.pdf import PdfConverter and keep the original API (create_model_dict, text_from_rendered, JSON block tree, etc.).
  • MinerU: Replace imports to from docling_rs.mineru.parser import parse and retain MinerU 4’s SDK (ParseResult, markdown(), JSON, Content Lists, save()).
  • Each compatibility guide includes side‑by‑side measurements (MarkItDown, Marker, MinerU).

🌐 Availability

  • Install with pip: pip install docling-rs.
  • Install with npm or from source checkout.
  • Download models once with: 
    1
2

    import docling_rs
docling_rs.download_models()
    or via download_dependencies.sh for non‑Python workflows.
  • Windows support documented in docs/WINDOWS.md.
  • Try the converter directly in the browser (WebAssembly, OCR included) at https://docling-project.github.io/docling.rs/ – processing stays on your device.

📚 Documentation

  • Detailed performance and profiling notes: ./docs/PDF_CONFORMANCE.md#performance--review--profiling-notes.
  • Model download instructions: see the Getting the ML models section referenced in the docs.
  • API migration guides for MarkItDown, Marker, and MinerU are linked in each bullet above.

#docling #Rust #documentconversion #LLM #RAG
